items.title: Section: Denying the Truths Denies Direct Sight Itself, and What Craving Actually Is

items.zh: 若於諸諦起損減執，彼於三量亦生誹謗。謂現量、比量及聖教量。亦謗染淨。是故說此名損減邊。若不墮在如是二邊，彼於諸諦能生信解，決定通達，漸次能證究竟清淨。云何苦諦？謂生苦等，廣說如前。若略說者，如說一切生雜染事，皆名苦諦。云何集諦？謂說一切煩惱雜染及業雜染，皆名集諦。世尊就勝，唯顯貪愛。
items.en: If one gives rise to the diminishing view towards these truths, one thereby slanders all three sources of knowledge, direct perception, inference, and scriptural authority, and slanders defiled and pure causation as well. Not falling into either extreme, one gains genuine confidence in the truths, decisively understands them, and gradually realises ultimate purity. What is the truth of suffering? Birth and its miseries, extensively explained already. Briefly stated, every event belonging to the defilement of rebirth is called the truth of suffering. What is the truth of origination? All affliction defilement and karma defilement together are called the truth of origination. The World-Honoured One, addressing what is supreme, singled out craving alone.

items.title: Section: Eight Kinds of Stillness, and the Eight Supports That Keep Ordinary Life Turning

items.zh: 云何滅諦？所謂一切煩惱永斷。又此永斷由八種相，如前應知。此中愛盡離欲者，此顯有餘依涅槃界。永滅涅槃者，此顯無餘依涅槃界。
items.en: What is the truth of cessation? The permanent severing of every affliction. This permanent severing unfolds through eight aspects, as already explained. Among these, the exhaustion of craving and freedom from desire reveal nirvana with residue; utter, final extinguishing reveals nirvana without residue.

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Path Gathered Into the Noble Eightfold Way

items.zh: 云何道諦？謂資糧道、若方便道、若清淨道，如是一切總略為一，說名道諦。世尊就勝，依能攝受沙門果證，但略顯示八聖支道名為道諦。
items.en: What is the truth of the path? The path of requisites, the preparatory path, and the path of purification, all gathered together and briefly named the truth of the path. The World-Honoured One, addressing what is supreme, in terms of embracing the realisation of the śramaṇa fruits, briefly revealed the noble eightfold path as the truth of the path.

items.title: Section: A Śrāvaka's Own Threefold Path, from Gathering Requisites to Final Purity

items.zh: 資糧道者，有十三種，如聲聞地已說應知。方便道者，若就最勝，謂於煗、頂、忍、世第一法位中，所有一切諸念住等菩提分法。清淨道者，謂於見道、修道、究竟道中，即彼所攝所有一切菩提分法。究竟道中，所有能引諸功德道，彼亦皆入道諦數中。
items.en: The path of requisites has thirteen kinds, already explained in the Grounds of Śrāvakas. The preparatory path, addressing what is supreme, names all the foundations of mindfulness and other factors of awakening cultivated at the stages of heat, summit, patience, and supreme worldly dharma. The path of purification names every factor of awakening belonging to the path of seeing, the path of cultivation, and the ultimate path. Whatever paths within the ultimate path draw forth excellent qualities are likewise counted among the truth of the path.

items.title: Section: The Bodhisattva's Own Path, and Why Suffering Is Always Named First

items.zh: 又諸菩薩方便道者，謂六波羅蜜多所攝。清淨道者，謂般若波羅蜜多所攝。此約最勝說，非不一切菩提分法皆遍修習。如世尊言：略五取蘊皆名苦者。此五取蘊若廣分別，如前意地決擇蘊善巧中，應知其相。又苦集諦略有三種，謂欲、色、無色繫差別故。又於十方無邊世界有差別故，其量無邊。對治此故，應知滅諦、道諦差別。
items.en: The bodhisattva's preparatory path is embraced within the six perfections. The path of purification is embraced within the perfection of wisdom. This is stated in terms of what is supreme; it is not that every factor of awakening is not also fully cultivated. The truths of suffering and origination are, briefly, of three kinds, according to their binding to the desire, form, and formless realms. Given the difference across the boundless worlds of the ten directions, their measure is truly boundless. Countering this, one should know the truths of cessation and the path differ in just the same way.

items.zh: 又此諸諦建立次第廣分別義，如前應知。復次，即此諸諦為據、為依、為建立處，立十三種補特伽羅。云何十三種補特伽羅？

items.title: Section: Thirteen Kinds of Person the Four Truths Establish

items.zh: 謂欲界異生、色界異生、無色界異生、欲界有學、色界有學、無色界有學、欲界無學、色界無學、無色界無學、欲界獨覺、欲界菩薩、色界菩薩、不可思議如來。
items.en: Ordinary beings of the desire, form, and formless realms; trainees of the desire, form, and formless realms; adepts of the desire, form, and formless realms; pratyekabuddhas of the desire realm; bodhisattvas of the desire realm; bodhisattvas of the form realm; and the inconceivable Tathāgata.

items.zh: 又即如是補特伽羅，若造作、若障、若心、若煩惱、若業、若根、若界、若信解、若意樂、若隨眠、若生、若習氣、若聚，皆應了知。

items.title: Section: Twelve Kinds of Conduct Behind Every Kind of Person

items.zh: 復次，造作者，有十二種。謂善造作、不善造作、無記造作、出家造作、彼勝流造作、彼防護造作、生造作、離欲造作、解脫造作、練根造作、引發神通造作、發起他義造作。
items.en: Furthermore, conduct is of twelve kinds: wholesome conduct, unwholesome conduct, neutral conduct, the conduct of renunciation, the conduct of that supreme stream, the conduct of guarding oneself, the conduct of seeking rebirth, the conduct of freedom from desire, the conduct of liberation, the conduct of refining the faculties, the conduct of drawing forth miraculous powers, and the conduct of benefiting others.

items.zh: 復次，障者，有十二種。一、業障。謂作五無間業故。二、習氣障。謂先數習諸惡業故。三、放逸障。謂大興盛現在前時，受用諸欲。四、蓋障。謂五種蓋隨一現前覆蔽其心。五、懈怠障。謂由懈怠少分煩惱纏擾其心。六、障礙障。謂十一種障礙隨一現前。七、生障。謂生無暇處。八、不生障。謂佛世尊不現於世。九、信解障。謂佛世尊雖現世間，而生邪見。

items.title: Section: Three Obstructions Only a Buddha Fully Escapes

items.zh: 十、煩惱障。謂由彼故，說慧解脫心得解脫。十一、定障。謂由彼故，說俱分解脫心得解脫。十二、所知障。謂由彼故，說諸如來心得解脫。復次，心者，略有二種。一、有障心，二、無障心。煩惱者，亦略有二種。謂纏及隨眠。業者，亦略有二種。謂思及思已。
items.en: Affliction obstruction is overcome through liberation by wisdom. Concentration obstruction is overcome through liberation in both respects. The cognitive obstruction: it is through freedom from it that the Tathāgatas' minds are said to be liberated. Mind is, briefly, of two kinds: obstructed mind and unobstructed mind. Affliction is likewise of two kinds: manifestation and latent tendency. Karma is likewise of two kinds: intention and intention already acted upon.

blocks.text: What happens when the truths are denied, and the kinds of person the truths establish.

Such a person slanders direct perception, inference, and scripture, and slanders the causation of both defilement and purity. Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering and origin are the cause and effect of defilement; cessation and the path, of purity. (Untranslated, 0655b17: the extreme of exaggeration, refuted: no self apart from the aggregates, nothing permanent; the extreme of diminishment: holding the truths to be without nature.)
All affliction and karma are origin; craving is named as supreme.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the noble path first gathers requisites, then applies preparation, then cultivates purity.
The six perfections belong to the preparatory path, the perfection of wisdom to purification.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the list really has fourteen items, but hearing and reflecting are joined. (Untranslated, 0655c25 and 0656a03: thirteen kinds of person are established on the truths, each to be understood by their karma, obstructions, mind, afflictions, faculties, and so on.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: to enter nirvāṇa one must draw near a good friend, hear the Dharma, attend correctly, and practise.

Master Cháng Bǎi: undefiled wisdom gives liberation by wisdom; concentration gives liberation of mind; freed of both obstructions, the Tathāgata's mind is called liberated. (Untranslated, 0656a11: twelve obstructions: the five heinous deeds, past habits, indulgence, the hindrances, laziness, eleven obstacles, birth without leisure, a buddha not appearing, wrong views even when he does.)
"A buddha not appearing" is listed among the obstructions. To meet the teaching at all is already a rare condition.

quiz.q: What does one slander by diminishing the truths?
options: the Three Jewels along with parents and teachers, since one who diminishes the truths trusts no authority at all
the three trainings of precepts, concentration, and wisdom
the three sources of knowledge, and defiled and pure causation as well
the desire, form, and formless realms
quiz.why: The treatise says such a person slanders direct perception, inference, and scriptural authority, and slanders defiled and pure causation. The definition of diminishment itself is missing from the English.

quiz.q: Why does diminishing the truths slander defilement and purity, says Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: because all four truths are pure and none is defiled, so that denying them denies purity
suffering alone is defiled; the rest are pure
suffering and origination are defiled cause and effect; cessation and path are pure
origination alone is pure; the rest are defiled
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering and origination are the cause and effect of defilement, and cessation and the path those of purity, so diminishing the truths at once slanders defiled and pure causation.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the Buddha singling out craving?
options: origination is craving alone, with no other affliction or karma in it
speaking of the strongest cause, craving is shown as the main cause of rebirth
craving is the easiest affliction to cut
craving is a habit that arhats retain
quiz.why: The treatise says all affliction and karma are origination, and craving is named as supreme. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha, speaking of the strongest and most influential cause, shows craving as the main cause of beings' rebirth.

quiz.q: Why, says Master Cháng Bǎi, is the noble path divided into three?
options: because three kinds of people differ, the dull taking one, the middling another
because each of the three realms has its own path
because each of the three trainings has its own path
one first gathers requisites, then uses preparation, and so cultivates purity
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the noble path must first gather requisites, then apply preparation, and so cultivate purity, which is why the truth of the path has three. They are stages in sequence, not alternatives for different people.

quiz.q: What does the treatise say of the bodhisattva's preparatory path and path of purification?
options: the preparatory is embraced in wisdom and purification in all six, since wisdom must come first and only the completed six are pure
the preparatory is the means of gathering; purification the immeasurables
the preparatory is embraced in the six perfections; purification in the perfection of wisdom
the preparatory is precepts; purification is concentration
quiz.why: The treatise assigns the six perfections to the preparatory path and the perfection of wisdom to the path of purification. It adds that this is stated in terms of what is supreme, not excluding other factors of awakening.

quiz.q: Which group appears among the twelve kinds of conduct?
options: the conduct of requisites, preparation, and purification, matching the three paths and so especially important in the twelve
the conduct of freedom from desire, of liberation, and of refining the faculties
the conduct of body, speech, and mind
the conduct of generosity, precepts, and patience
quiz.why: The treatise lists wholesome, unwholesome, neutral, renunciation, that supreme stream, guarding, rebirth, freedom from desire, liberation, refining the faculties, miraculous powers, and benefiting others. The other groups are not on the list.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say 勝 means in the conduct of that supreme stream?
options: 勝 is nirvana; one enters it by good friends, hearing, attention, and practice
勝 is a fine body, for this conduct brings excellent marks
勝 is victory over other paths
勝 is a supreme heavenly place
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 勝 refers to nirvana, and to enter nirvana one must draw near a good friend, hear the true Dharma, bring correct attention, and practice in accordance with the Dharma, the same four practices stated at the start of the fascicle.

quiz.q: "The path of requisites has fourteen kinds" renders 有十三種. What has happened?
options: the English is right: thirteen is a copying slip since the Śrāvaka Grounds list fourteen
a wrong number: the text says thirteen, hearing and reflection being counted as one
the English also counts the four preparations
fourteen adds the path of purification
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the list really has fourteen items, but hearing and reflecting on the Dharma are joined into one, so it is stated as thirteen. The treatise here says thirteen, and the English number disagrees with its own Chinese.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain liberation in both respects?
options: both body and mind are freed, meaning that afflictions end just as the body is left at death
freed of both the affliction and cognitive obstructions
undefiled wisdom is liberation by wisdom; concentration is liberation of mind; both are freed
both householders and renunciants are freed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: gaining undefiled wisdom through the noble path is liberation by wisdom, and gaining concentration is liberation of mind; when both are freed it is called liberation in both respects. Freedom from both obstructions is the Buddha's.

quiz.q: This is rendered "overcome only by the Tathāgatas' own mind." What is the problem?
options: the sense is that freed of it the Tathāgata's mind is said to be liberated; only is added
nothing: only the Tathāgata's mind has the strength to overcome it
it should be overcome by arhats
所知障 should be affliction
quiz.why: The clause says that this obstruction being gone, the Tathāgata's mind is called liberated. Master Cháng Bǎi: being freed of both obstructions is called Buddha. The mind is not an agent here, and the word only is added.
